Retain the author's Physics model: **8 heads × 32 channels = width 256**, **5 local / 4 global layers**, ReLU variant, shared Q/K, beta=-1, no pre-LN, feature normalization through `NormalizeFeatures`, native self-loop/edge treatment, Adam lr=.001, decay=.0005, input dropout=.1 and local/global dropout=.5. Raw FP32 Physics features alone occupy about **1.08 GiB**. One four-member width-256 node-state tensor occupies **135 MiB**. One materialized per-edge width-256 message occupies **484 MiB per member per layer**; five local layers × four members could retain about **9.46 GiB** of such messages before other activations, gradients and input-dropout/scaling copies. Boundary sharing saves weight storage, not these member-dependent activations.

A possible *changed* initializer has an explicit definition: for training graphs only, lift graph loss through the real readout/pooling Jacobian to node-hidden cotangents `t = ∂L_graph/∂h`; apply a block-diagonal within-graph band filter to t; pull back with the node-encoder/private-factor Jacobian. **Newman and Leicht (2007), method only, PDF pages 2–4, Eqs. (1)–(13).** A node has one latent class whose globally shared preference vector explains all its observed outgoing neighbours. With class weights \(\pi_r\), attachment preferences \(\theta_{rj}\), and adjacency \(A\), the written likelihood contains \(\prod_i\pi_{g_i}\prod_j\theta_{g_i,j}^{A_{ij}}\). Its posterior responsibility is proportional to \(\pi_r\prod_j\theta_{rj}^{A_{ij}}\); its preference update is \(\theta_{rj}=\sum_i A_{ij}q_{ir}/\sum_i k_iq_{ir}\). This is attachment-preference likelihood algebra, not the current exact fixed-cardinality binary-subset law or an audited Bernoulli whole-graph density.
